question: What primary group of healthcare workers administers the vast majority of injections in clinical settings?
explanation: Nurses form the frontline of healthcare delivery and administer most parenteral medications daily. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h1)

question: Injection safety focuses on preventing harm during which part of healthcare?
explanation: Injection safety focuses specifically on measures taken during the preparation and administration of medicines through injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do some clinics reuse disposable syringes when supplies are low?

options.B: New syringe technology makes it easy
options.D: There are too many medical supplies

explanation: Shortages of basic medical equipment often force clinics to reuse single-use items improperly. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient demands an injection instead of tablets for a mild fever because of a local belief. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Give a double dose of antibiotics
options.B: Set up an IV line immediately
options.C: Reuse a clean syringe to save clinic stock
options.D: Teach the patient about how well oral drugs work

explanation: Patient preferences driven by misconceptions are best addressed through health education rather than giving unnecessary injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which practice is a major safety violation when using multi-dose medication vials?

options.A: Leaving a needle stuck in the vial rubber top
options.B: Wiping the rubber top with alcohol
options.C: Writing the date the vial was opened on it
options.D: Storing the vial according to the maker's rules

explanation: Leaving a needle in a vial provides an open pathway for germs from the environment to contaminate the remaining medication. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is it unsafe to change just the needle while reusing the same syringe barrel?

options.A: It makes the new needle tip blunt very quickly
options.B: It increases the cost of materials for the hospital
options.C: Blood or body fluids stay inside the syringe barrel and plunger
options.D: Syringe barrels melt when used a second time

explanation: Fluid flowing back into the barrel during use contaminates the inside, making it unsafe for another patient even if a fresh needle is attached. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which bloodborne virus has the highest risk of spreading after a single accidental needle-stick injury?
explanation: Hepatitis B has a high concentration of viral particles in the blood, making transmission very efficient after an exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h4)

question: How do germs usually spread during an unsafe injection?

options.A: Breathing in air droplets while drawing up medicine
options.B: Eating food handled by infected staff
options.D: Directly injecting contaminated blood or fluids into the body

explanation: Unsafe injections bypass the natural skin barrier, directly introducing infectious agents into tissues or the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h4)

question: Long-term Hepatitis B or C infection from unsafe injections often leads to which condition?
explanation: Hepatitis B and C primarily attack liver cells, leading over time to chronic inflammation, scarring, and cirrhosis. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h5)

question: How do complications from unsafe injections usually affect low-income households financially?

options.A: They reduce money spent on regular drugs
options.B: They cause high medical bills that can lead to financial ruin
options.C: They increase cash flow through insurance payouts
options.D: They provide free long-term care services

explanation: Paying out-of-pocket for severe infections and long-term treatments can quickly drain family savings. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which group of healthcare workers experiences the most accidental needle-stick injuries?
explanation: Nurses handle and throw away the vast majority of needles and sharps daily, which increases their risk of exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is a key action required right after an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Throwing away the needle without testing
options.C: Stopping all clinical work for six months
options.D: Writing an annual hospital incident report

explanation: Prompt assessment and timely post-exposure care can significantly reduce the risk of getting a viral infection. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the recommended safe way to recap a used needle if it is absolutely necessary?

options.A: Using both hands to twist the cap on
options.B: Holding the cap in your mouth
options.C: Pressing the cap on with your palm

explanation: The one-handed scoop technique prevents your free hand from getting accidentally poked during cap replacement. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why are single-dose medication vials preferred over multi-dose vials for infection control?

options.A: They need special refrigerators for storage
options.B: They are much more expensive to make
options.C: They stop germs from spreading between patients

explanation: Single-dose vials are thrown away after one use, preventing the accidental introduction of germs into multiple doses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: At what level should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced?
explanation: Sealing sharps boxes at three-quarters capacity prevents needles from sticking out and poking people during handling. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h8)

question: Where should a sharps disposal box be placed in a clinical ward?

options.A: Within arm's reach of where injections are prepared
options.B: Outside the building near the incinerator

explanation: Placing sharps containers close to the point of use stops staff from walking across rooms with exposed needles. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is the main goal of having a blame-free reporting system for needle-stick injuries?

options.A: To spend less money on safety boxes
options.B: To publicly punish staff who make mistakes
options.C: To remove the need for safety committees
options.D: To encourage staff to report quickly and get prompt medical care

explanation: A blame-free environment removes the fear of punishment, ensuring staff report incidents fast to receive timely medical checks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: A nurse notices the clinic keeps running out of safety boxes, causing staff to recap needles unsafely. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Ignore the problem since management should handle it
options.B: Use cardboard boxes as permanent replacements
options.C: Tell patients to stop taking injections
options.D: Report the supply shortage to hospital management and ask for action

explanation: Nurses must speak up for essential safety resources to protect both patients and healthcare workers from avoidable harm. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)
